newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RGC says Sierra Leone coup setback for mine.
newsitem.headline: RGC says Sierra Leone coup setback for mine.

text.p: Efforts to re-establish mineral sand mining in Sierra Leone has suffered a setback from a coup which has toppled the troubled African nation's year-old elected government, mine partner RGC Ltd said on Monday.

"It is fair to categorise the most recent events in Sierra Leone as a setback to efforts to get the mine back up," Keith Faulkner, general manager of RGC's RGC Mineral Sands Ltd division told Reuters. However, Faulkner said it was too early to determine the impact of the coup on the mine's future.
"To say we know anything more today than yesterday would be impossible right now," he told Reuters from Geraldton, Western Australia, where RGC's mineral sands division is based.
The mine was overrun by rebels in January 1995.

Sierra Rutile and its two shareholders, Consolidated Rutile Ltd and Nord Resources (Corp) of the United States, have been evaluating the mine and market opportunities for mineral sand since resecuring the mine in January 1996, Faulkner said.
The companies each own a 50 percent stake in the mine.
Consolidated Rutile is 50.1 percent owned by Cudgen RZ Ltd, which in turn is about 77 percent owned by RGC.
Soldiers seized power in Sierra Leone on Sunday.
